item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Thursday, 20 August 2026
item.description:
Aywren finally clicks with Balatro after learning to spend early, turning a baffling poker roguelike into a four-hour Steam Deck-friendly rabbit hole.

Krista’s early take on Life is Strange: Double Exposure is warm on older Max, the two-timeline mystery, and an opening chapter that hooks nicely.

Shintar revisits WoW Midnight housing with softened edges: still flawed, but collecting decor and guild house visits add some genuine charm.

Wilhelm sizes up Stars Reach’s Steam Early Access launch: decent crafting foundations, no spaceships yet, and MMO server realities pushing the price above survival-game norms.

Andrew Plotkin reads GDC 2027’s cheaper expo and new business hall as a practical pivot, not exactly the pure B2B future the branding claims.

Anarchae writes powerfully about life under constant cameras, from workplace surveillance to influencers, Meta Glasses, and the exhaustion of never really opting out.

Aneesh bookmarks The Tarpa Player, a music-related YouTube find, with no extra commentary beyond the pointer.

Tipa checks in on Kickstarter backs, from Battlestations: Lightspeed’s family-friendly six-player promise to the trillo wind controller’s quiet, recorder-shaped musical appeal.

Roger looks back on podcasting’s shift from scrappy Audacity-and-Skype fandom to polished video-first productions that feel slicker but less soulful.

Cristian drops a blunt minimalist thought: most of us are storing stuff at home we don’t need or haven’t touched in years.

Axxuy shares a candid Blaugust slump update, with low energy and few posts, but still cheers the month’s wider burst of blogging creativity.

Welsh Troll hits Blaugust’s midpoint with encouragement, some honest pacing struggles, and a newly found static-site archive bug to fix.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Wednesday, 19 August 2026
item.description:
Syp is happily poking through LOTRO’s Yondershire, eyeing Wolves of Mordor, and maybe easing back into regular blogging without making it a whole thing.

Cliffski is redesigning Ridiculous Space Battles’ challenge browser, chasing the sweet spot between clean UI and his beloved gloriously overstuffed data dashboard.

Frostilyte’s low-tier Pokémon Silver run gets a huge boost from Headbutt and the elemental punches, with Vanessa suddenly turning into a menace.

Kimimi digs into FromSoftware’s PSP Adventure Player, a spooky little platform for user-made adventure games that thankfully still makes sideloading delightfully easy.

Marc spotlights MUSHA as a brilliantly named Aleste detour, where samurai-flavored mechs and ‘Edo metal’ give the shooter a killer identity.

Wilhelm’s Planet Crafter crew hit full automation hell, where drones, auto crafters, trade rockets, and portals turn abundance into a storage-management comedy.

Ramen Junkie rounds up Transformers Swapticons and finds the gimmick neat in theory, but the samey, kinda-ugly designs don’t exactly inspire completionism.

Tim Bray makes the Wilcox prairie look anything but boring, with big Saskatchewan skies, harvest fields, and a photographer’s eye for cloud drama.

Tipa checks in on The Guns of Navarone, enjoying the old-school WWII adventure while side-eyeing its square-jawed heroics and one suspiciously familiar Barry.

Jeff gives Raspberry Pi’s CM5 Programming Jig a first pass, and it looks like a much saner way to provision piles of Compute Modules.

Mike starts porting Tetris to the BBC Bridge Companion, using MAME and a lot of Z80 map-reading before real hardware enters the picture.

Owls marks Whyday by remembering _why the lucky stiff and making the case for programming as play, not just EnterpriseFactoryBeanFactoryFactory drudgery.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 18 August 2026
item.description:
Sey is all-in on Mina the Hollower, praising its Link’s Awakening throwback feel, Soulsy challenge, secrets, and burrowing twist.

Azuriel revisits hazy NES memories, from Super Mario Bros. 3 and Zelda II to Blaster Master and the wrong game arriving at Christmas.

Scopique digs Riftborne, a cheap terminal-window 4X with ASCII vibes, sharp upkeep mechanics, and exactly the kind of menu-heavy old-school friction he wants.

Wilhelm says Blaugust hasn’t changed his approach much: he’s still logging his gaming life, not chasing guides, reviews, or whatever the RSS argument is.

Home sick with COVID, The Friendly Necromancer spends the day soloing Nagafen and Lady Vox in EverQuest Legends and hauling off some tasty loot.

Ghastly tours WoW’s Ironforge, pokes around the Explorers’ Guild, handles dwarf errands, and wraps Dun Morogh with a dead bear and level 13.

Tobold says Pathfinder: Wrath of the Righteous buries players in loot they can’t really use once weapon specialization locks a party into narrow builds.

Michael revisits co-open with his kids and loves how its no-pressure grocery-store wandering sparks exploration, roleplay, and made-up stories.

Bhagpuss spins a questionnaire post into a ramble on interviews, newspapers, The Guardian, and discovering Lana Del Rey through “Video Games.”

Brennan responds to circlejerk.blog parodying the IndieWeb scene, crediting the mimicry while chewing over what the satire gets right and wrong.

Bruce Schneier flags two papers arguing LLM memory still leaks sensitive context too easily, and that better reasoning beats just prompt-fiddling.

Tipa looks back on CP/M and FlexOS at DRI, then wonders how close she came to the future Maxis business-sim branch of history.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 17 August 2026
item.description:
Ocho is having a great time with ESO’s Return of the Thieves Guild, especially the sneaky rewards, Sheogorath weirdness, and cheese-fueled questing.

Nimgimli liked Diablo IV’s story and monster-smooshing, but Lord of Hate lost him with platform-locked expansion access and unreliable quest progress saves.

Shintar digs into SWTOR 8.0 finally getting the name Masters of the Force, plus confirmation that Galaxy in Chaos brings new story content.

Luna is sold on Hips N Noses’ bold art, funny banter, and clever mashup of cafe management with Vampire Survivors-style dream combat.

Joar says WoW: Shadowlands finally made him quit, thanks to covenant math, Maw and Torghast chores, anima grind, and a story payoff that soured.

Wilhelm’s Fantasy Critic League update is mostly a holding pattern, with Marvel Tokon and Pokemon Pokopia finally posting scores before a quiet August stretch.

The Chronicler highlights Army of the Potomac as a low-complexity GMT Civil War wargame with quick scenarios, campaign rules, and big-picture tactical depth.

Tipa rounds up a mixed movie binge, from Satanist-hotel horror-comedy and Old Henry to Fast and Furious confusion and a Hunger Games prequel bail-out.

Blockade85 writes candidly about feeling out of sync at 35, grieving lost years, and no longer feeling at home in games like Destiny 2 and FFXIV.

Juhis makes a brisk case for Django ORM, arguing it beats raw SQL for modeling business logic and quick database poking in the shell.

Kelly hits 31 Blaugust posts, crediting brevity and borrowed inspiration, while admitting the pace was exhausting and probably a one-time thing.

Joel shares his Blaugust reading list, spotlighting bloggers covering patient gaming, planned obsolescence, games, tech, books, and indie web journeys.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 16 August 2026
item.description:
Stargrace briefly rerolls from a level 50 bard to a level 40 enchanter, then bails to wait for a patch boosting group experience.

Magi resurfaces a Gamescom interview on Eldritch Empathy, where Lovecraftian roguelike encounters trade reflex combat for Papers, Please-style empathy puzzles.

Wes digs into PCSX2-Reliquary, a fork tackling PS2 oddities and finally making Stuntman playable at full speed, even on Steam Deck.

Ellie dives back into Blasphemous II and finds its grim Catholic-horror metroidvania vibe still hits hard after the first game.

Wilhelm looks back over 13 years of Blaugust, from Belghast’s 2014 daily-post challenge through the community’s evolving rhythms.

Wolfy checks in 10 days into Blaugust, feeling tired but steady, and treating the whole thing as a time-management crucible.

Anarchae’s weekly digest rounds up Backrest backups, Picard music cleanup, sci-fi and mysteries, Traitors AU, new music, and Zelda.

Warner savors the early-morning stillness at the lake, with quiet water and the occasional fish jump doing the heavy lifting.

Jamie Zawinski flags a grim archival-data mess, with Nine PBS suing over lost access to 70 years of material held in storage limbo.

Dave Winer reflects on tech collaboration, arguing software interop is easy compared to the harder part: people actually wanting to work together.

Tan gives a friendly primer on tangent spaces, manifolds, charts, and geometry, with Earth and video game level analogies keeping it grounded.

Wakupan shows off a writing setup built around a Lofree Flow Lite keyboard, Logicool Lift mouse, Rollbahn notebooks, and favorite desk companions.
